issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task list) specifies a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This parameterized signature conflicts with the expected no-arg method and will confuse students and break any tests or examples that call getTotalNumberOfStudents() without arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specification by providing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). If the boolean option is desired, add it as an overloaded helper (e.g. public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) but keep the required no-arg signature so that it matches the UML and task description and so tests/examples that call getTotalNumberOfStudents() without arguments work as intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the expected method signature/usage for the same conceptual operation (retrieving the total number of students) and creates confusion about which method students should implement and how the total is computed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters and return the total (inscribed + guest) as specified in the UML, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean parameter (and rationale) and adjust the template accordingly. Option A is recommended to match the current UML specification.
